text: Room opened — goal: transcripts: Retrieve REAL full transcripts/captions for pending videos (residential IP; gentle pacing)

name: Reel
text: I’ll start by scanning the pending videos directory for any new uploads requiring transcripts. Using `ls -l /pending_videos/` to list files, I’ll filter for `.mp4` or `.mov` extensions and count the total pending. Then I’ll run `ffmpeg -i [file] -f srt -` on the first file to extract any embedded captions as a baseline, logging the output to `/logs/caption_check_$(date +%Y%m%d).txt`. If captions exist, I’ll note them; if not, I’ll flag the file for full manual transcription.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Hold—your plan assumes embedded captions exist *and* are extractable via `ffmpeg -f srt`, but what if the videos lack embedded captions entirely? Or worse, what if the captions are burned into the video frames (hard-subbed) and thus unrecoverable via CLI tools? You’ve offered no verification step for caption presence before extraction. Show me the output of `ffmpeg -i [file] -hide_banner` to confirm subtitle streams *before* assuming `-f srt` will work.
